rationales: Agriculture is an applied field, but it is not usually identified as the latest profession of biology.
Horticulture is the cultivation of plants, not the latest profession of biology.
Farming is an occupation rather than the latest profession of biology.
Biotechnology is commonly described as the latest profession or field of biology.
One FADH₂ is traditionally credited with producing 2 ATP in the textbook convention.
This is the expected textbook yield from one FADH₂.
Three ATP is the traditional yield from NADH, not FADH₂.
Four ATP is not the accepted textbook yield from one FADH₂.
Melvin Calvin received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1961.
Calvin did not receive the Nobel Prize in 1962.
Calvin did not receive the Nobel Prize in 1963.
Calvin did not receive the Nobel Prize in 1964.
Lipids are not the main substance of which enzymes are made.
Almost all enzymes are proteins.
Carbohydrates are not the main substance of which enzymes are made.
Nucleic acids are not the main substance of which enzymes are made.
Metabolism is not derived from Latin.
Metabolism comes from the Greek word meaning change or transformation.
Metabolism is not derived from Italian.
Metabolism is not derived from English.
Karl Lohmann is credited with discovering ATP.
Fritz Lipmann contributed to the understanding of ATP and its role, but did not discover it.
Calvin is known for work on the photosynthetic carbon cycle, not ATP's discovery.
Darwin did not discover ATP.
NADH is produced during glycolysis but is not the molecule into which glucose is split.
FADH₂ is not produced as the direct breakdown product of glucose in glycolysis.
Glycolysis breaks one glucose molecule down into two molecules of pyruvic acid.
Acetyl coenzyme A is formed from pyruvic acid after glycolysis.
85% is not the stated textbook percentage of saturated fatty acids in butter.
80% is not the stated textbook percentage of saturated fatty acids in butter.
75% is not the stated textbook percentage of saturated fatty acids in butter.
The expected textbook answer is that butter contains about 70% saturated fatty acids.
Histology is the study of tissues, not external structures of organisms.
Morphology is the study of the form and external structures of organisms.
Anatomy primarily concerns the internal structure of organisms.
Microbiology is the study of microscopic organisms.
Hydrogen makes up about 10% of the human body by mass in the textbook composition figures.
14% is not the stated percentage of hydrogen in the body.
12% is not the stated percentage of hydrogen in the body.
18% is closer to the stated percentage of carbon, not hydrogen.
Male Anopheles mosquitoes do not transmit malaria in sparrows.
Female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit human malaria, not the malaria referred to in sparrows.
Culex mosquitoes are the stated vectors of malaria in sparrows.
Aedes mosquitoes are not the stated vectors of malaria in sparrows.
Algae are not assigned to kingdom Fungi in this classification.
Monera includes prokaryotes, not the algae referred to here.
Animalia comprises animals, not algae.
Algae are assigned to kingdom Protista in this classification.
The human body is commonly described as having about 200 types of cells.
225 is not the commonly cited count of human cell types.
300 is not the commonly cited count of human cell types.
350 is not the commonly cited count of human cell types.
G₂ is part of interphase, before spindle fibers form during mitosis.
Interphase precedes mitosis and is not the phase in which the spindle forms.
Spindle fibers begin forming during prophase.
Metaphase is when chromosomes line up at the cell equator, after spindle formation.
Mountain-ebony is the common name for Bauhinia variegata.
Allium cepa is onion.
Asterias rubens is a starfish.
Pisum sativum is the garden pea.
